speaker: rickhilderley
text: The quick synopsis is that we have a plan for instruction for the 2020-21 school year. It includes basically three tiers or three choices for parents. One is the virtual option through the Tecumseh Virtual Academy that we are calling the anytime, anywhere teaching and learning approach. One thing that will keep that similar to the curriculum that the district will be using is Edmentum's assessment tool that will give us first-of-the-year data. Then we're going to do that across the board for all students, regardless of if they're in the virtual academy or not. Then we're going to use that at the end of the year as well, similar to what we have done with NWEA in the past. We're just not going to do that. The tool is already in Edmentum. Not purchasing the NWEA testing will save us some money in the general fund. That's helpful. The other option is to be online, but this is for families who will be planning to come back in the district for instruction at some point. If the pandemic is brought to phase six because of a vaccine or therapeutics, then they may want to return with their cohort into live instruction. The caveat there is that the parents will have to agree that their students are on our schedule. They will have to attend daily and they'll have breaks for their specials like our gym and music and things like that all online. Our instructor will be in our facility and then the students would be at home in a cohort throughout the school year until there's a time when we're ready to bring that group back in. Then thirdly is the in-person option. In all of these options, technology is going to be utilized to a great extent. We have to anticipate that at some point once we're face-to-face that there could be positive cases. There could be government mandates that push us back to phase three and we would all have to go home for instruction. If any of those things happen, we've got to have technology in the hands of the youngest learners that don't involve a keyboard because they're just learning their alphabet in some cases. I asked Evan to get a price for 500 chrome touchpads and he was able to do that rather quickly. The price is good until the 22nd of August, but in order to get them delivered so that we can use them when school starts, I couldn't wait until the 10th of August to bring this to the regular board meeting. I believe that you've seen the quote that involves the devices and cases to keep them safe and we would be using them for both in-person and

speaker: kevinjohnson
text: distance learning. All right. Also, I think all the board members got the revised budget, which wasn't a big revision.
